text:
sophia: noticed a couple of postmortem actions have been aging out with no clear owners. can we formalize the follow-up pipeline so things don't get lost?

brad: yes please. what's the smallest change that'll make a difference?

sophia: 3 small changes: (1) require a single owner per action (no team-level 'ops review'), (2) set a max TTL for each priority, (3) add a very lightweight visible board (not buried in docs).

nora: TTLs = good. propose: P1 = 7 days for a remediation plan + owner within 12h, P2 = 21 days for plan + owner within 48h, P3 = 90 days for plan + owner within 7 days. these are inclusive of weekends.

kevin: 90d for P3 seems long, but ok for biz-as-usual items. can we add auto-escalation after half the TTL if no progress?

sophia: yes. escalation points at 50% and 100% TTL. first escalation notifies the IC + manager, second escalates to reliability lead.

brad: board idea: a tiny CSV stored in repo + GH issues tagged incident-remediation. that lets us query and use PRs to change status.

nora: love that. sample CSV columns: id, owner, short_action, incident, priority, created, due, status, recurrence_tag, notes.

kevin: also suggest adding a 'stability-impact' column (low/med/high) so triage meeting can sort by business impact, not just priority.

sophia: good call. also: recurring pattern detection. instead of 90d window, use a rolling 120-day window and flag subsystem if >= 3 incidents or >= 2 P1s. then we schedule a reliability spike.

brad: can the board surface a "recurrence_tag" automatically? maybe a small script that scans incidents and appends tags.

oncall-bot: automation note: created label "incident-remediation" and a scheduled job to scan issue links daily.

nora: comms cadence suggestion:
- incident close: create postmortem + add actions to CSV + assign owner
- 48h check: owner confirms plan or moves to backlog with reason
- weekly 20-minute triage: review overdue/high-stability-impact items only
- 30/60/120-day review for pattern analysis

kevin: question: who owns long-running follow-ups after the original IC's attention window ends?

sophia: idea: original IC remains the 'short-term lead' for 72h post-close to handoff and confirm POA. after 72h, if still open, tasks move to a "remediation rotation". rotation members pick up items in a FIFO manner.

brad: rotation logistics: 2-week shifts with 2 on-call remediators per week. they do triage and pick any items older than 7 days or with high stability-impact.

nora: require a 1-line handoff note when rotating: reason for handoff, last actions, next known blocker. tiny but crucial for context.

kevin: add a template for handoff and for creating remediation GH issues. I'll draft both.

sophia: action items from this thread:
- brad: add incident-remediation label + CSV schema to repo by Fri
- kevin: draft GH issue + handoff templates by Thu
- nora: run a one-off scan for open postmortem actions and seed the board (assigning owners where obvious)
- sophia: write short process doc and publish to #eng-docs

brad: noted. will ping when CSV is live.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: will ping owners at 50% TTL and at overdue. See https://github.com/redwood-inference/incidents/boards/8

sophia: ok if nobody objects i'll roll these into the incident playbook. low friction is the north star here  keep the process lean so folks actually use it. :thumbsup:
